notes.title: Yai Gameworks 10-Year Anniversary Developer Stream & Sale
notes.content: [p]Hey! It's window of the 10-year anniversary of Yai Gameworks! I've officially been making little horror games for 10 years now! Three things to express here.[/p][p][/p][p]Firstly, all of the Yai Gameworks games are on sale on Steam right now at the cheapest prices they've ever been at for the Yai Gameworks 10-year anniversary. Sale lasts until September 1st, and I'll mention after this sale there will be a price increase for Decaying Delicacy & Feast Your Eyes ahead of their big updates, alongside Close Me's New Game+ DLC will be delisted from Steam (due to a shortly coming update to add all the New Game+ content to the base game, alongside some new random events), though those who've bought it will give a little exclusive alt costume in-game as thanks for those who supported and bought it.[/p][p]Can find all the games I've released on Steam here, all on sale for the Yai Gameworks 10-Year Anniversary Sale until September 1st, 2025:[/p][p][url="https://store.steampowered.com/search/?developer=Yai%20Gameworks"]https://store.steampowered.com/search/?developer=Yai%20Gameworks[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Second, tomorrow, August 22nd, at 11 AM PST / 2 PM EST / 6 PM GMT, I'll be holding a 10-year anniversary developer stream for Yai Gameworks, giving history, developer insight, fun facts & other surprises for the whole history of my horror games so far. Will be a VOD saved afterward if miss it, I have a lot of cool stuff to show. Can catch the stream here:[/p][previewyoutube="9xBiuMLHLuA;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Finally, sorry for this, but be a small delay to some of the plans. My grandmother had recently moved due to circumstances with her health, and she's now also fallen sick. Worrying since she's on an oxygen machine to help supply air to her brain because her body isn't producing enough. Me and my immediate family have set a trip to visit her from August 26th to November 3rd. I don't have a laptop or means to really work on my game during this, so going to change my plans a bit. Feast Your Eyes big update will be delayed to somewhere in September, Close Me update still happening in September, Inferbito release will be pushed to November, and Red Haze final update should still be December. Sorry for the quick announcement-delay, just grandmother stuff suddenly came into the picture which sorta' took away from my plans and deciding better to delay them a bit rather than rush everything along. I hope it's understandable.[/p][p][/p][p]Speaking of which, in November, I'll be releasing a new game called Inferbito. Much more news for it in September/October:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1624490/Inferbito/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]I hope you guys are having a wonderful day, and hope some of you will check out the stream either as its live or afterward in the VOD. Working hard and hope to surprise all of you with that, the upcoming free updates, and Inferbito. Toodles~[/p]

notes.title: Yai Gameworks 10-year anniversary; releasing FREE updates to all of my games!
notes.content:
Hey! Did you know we're approaching Yai Gameworks 10-year anniversary? Well, now you do! I've technically been making games since 2013, starting with Blank Slate, but "Yai Gameworks" was made officially in 2015 as part of becoming a Steam developer to release Close Your Eyes: Redux on Steam.

So I have some surprises for y'all! I'm doing a HUGE 10-year celebration. What does that entail? I'm going to update every single game I've released on Steam. This will start in a few days from now, but the updates will roll out through the next 477 days (until August 31st, 2026).

I will not reveal everything I'm adding to these games here, just the core new additions. I will give no ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) on any of these, just know that I'll post an update on each game's store page when each one is out (or of course, keep the game installed to be notified when the game updates). All of these updates will be FREE to owners of the games (and free updates to the already free games).

Here's the full list of what I'll be doing (along with store links to each one):

[b]Close Your Eyes [Old Version]:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/377330/Close_Your_Eyes_Old_Version/

Adding a new 9th ending, as well as updating the tech side of the game to play a bit nicer with newer PCs.

[b]Take the Dream IX:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/428870/Take_the_Dream_IX/

Getting a new ending added, achievements, and updated tech to play nicer with newer PCs.

[b]Red Haze:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/428860/Red_Haze/

Final update with Ending A, the A-Z Door, new secrets and random events added. The game will finally be complete!

[b]Close Me:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/671980/Close_Me/

I'm going to delist the "New Game+" DLC and make it part of the main game (+OST), add new random events, get a new ending, previous owners of the DLC will get a new costume as thanks for supporting.

[b]Twisted Puzzle DLC for Close Your Eyes [Old Version]:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/645840/Close_Your_Eyes__The_Twisted_Puzzle/

Will get a new second launch option w/remixed puzzles and extended Ending A, from CYE Remake ported over, to preserve it before a huge reimagining in CYER.

[b]Please Love My Computer Game:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/796910/Please_Love_My_Computer_Game/

Getting a new .exe file added to its files...

[b]Found Horror Game 11.exe:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/727720/Found_Horror_Game_11exe/

Getting Steam Trading Cards, Game 1 "Attendant" and Game 6 "Ominous Whisperer" are both getting huge updates, Game 8 "In Pale Moon I Saw Her Smile" will be released.

[b]Close Your Eyes Remake:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/706710/Close_Your_Eyes/

Big update coming to the game adding a lot to "Close Your Eyes", "Girl's Graveyard", "My Hole is a Mouth of Dirt: Director's Cut", and "Girls Graveyard Mystery", alongside a new Demo for the game released.

[b]Feast Your Eyes:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/712260/Feast_Your_Eyes/

A HUGE overhaul of Acts 1 & 2 (like, actually a big overhaul that'll add a lot of new content, rework previous areas), and going to release Act 3 so the game finally finished!

[b]Red Haze: Bruises Glimmer in Starlight DLC:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1553270/Red_Haze__Bruises_Glimmer_in_Starlight/

Gonna' try to fix a few things from the base game, and add a brand new second chapter!


[b]Decaying Delicacy:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1488540/Decaying_Delicacy/

A HUGE overhaul and update to make the game a Director's Cut version of itself; adds a LOT of new and reworked content into the game. Price of the game when the update hits will raise by $1 USD, and will finally release the OST of the game as well. Also Steam Achievements. This overhaul is actually huge as I think the game deserves to be so much more than it was.

[b]The Miserable Crimson Hooded Girl:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/667270/The_Miserable_Crimson_Hooded_Girl/

Adds a new mini-campaign you can play after you've beaten the game once, also Steam achievements added.


---


There we go. Again, NO ETA for these and will just randomly drop them (with an update to the store pages when they drop) over the next 477 days (to August 31st, 2026), but the first one of these updates happens this week. I hope y'all enjoy~!

Small update to just fix a few small bugs.

-Fixed it so you can leave the Forest Warehouse if you have 5 or 6 talismans.
-Fixed a bug where the game would crash in the Warehouse if you last input a blue button code incorrectly.
-Fixed the hit detection of the dumpster in My Hole is a Mouth of Dirt.
-A hypothetical attempt to fix a bug where you'd automatically when the "Spider" death zone in the doodily train section if you entered it a second time.

Happy New Years everyone!

notes.title: Close Your Eyes Version 0.3 Out Now!
notes.content:
Close Your Eyes Remake has updated to version 0.3!

This update while a relatively big one, didn't end up quite as fully cooked as I desired. This mostly ends up being an update adding more to content already in the game. Some of that content is practically all new; Some rooms have been completely reworked, there's various visual and audio additions, new flavor text added, new secrets, new surprises, and more. This has been more an "Art Final Pass" update than anything.

But that doesn't mean there isn't any new content, in fact all the WIP game modes outside of A Ghastly Tale have a small update to get to their next save point with new rooms, cutscenes, surprises, etc. But the next update will have to be the one that really expands on adding more content in a linear story fashion to the current dead ends that exist.

Before the full patch notes, here's three things I'm aware of:
-Not all of Mole's dialogue is voiced. In particular, there's a bit in the chapel cutscene and a bit in the God's Cradle cutscene where he's missing dialogue. This will be fixed in either the next update or the update after that; I need to do another recording session with his VA is the short of it.
-The Scarecrow Secret in Close Your Eyes is currently roadblocked as I didn't get it done in time.
-Similarly, the Girl's Graveyard second secret ending is currently roadblocked as I didn't get it done in time.

Now, with all of this said, here's the full patch notes!


GENERAL:
-The Marshmallow Monk sprite has been redone to look nicer, hope y'all like it!
-Added a new Screen Brightness adjuster to the settings menu.
-Added a fix for high refresh rate monitors for timing bugs.
-Updated some of the Steam Achievement Art and added a few more achievements (an Art Pass for all existing Steam Achievements will be next update, but a few achievements got an art pass this update).
-Fixed a Screen Resolution bug where there were two 720x528 options, added a 1600 x 900 resolution option instead.
-Fixed various file names for other language computers to read the files hopefully without errors.


THE ANNEX:
-The Annex Prologue added (just launch the Annex to experience it, supposed to be the first thing new players experience).
-Game posters/logos and the symbols above doors updated to be more readable and thematically fitting.
-Music player has some songs changed for the Annex Lobby.
-If you beat Girl's Graveyard, there's now a new thing that'll get added to the Annex Lobby you can play around with.


CLOSE YOUR EYES:
-Re-recorded various Host lines to their hopefully final form for the remake. Biggest changes are in the first cutscene in the game, the "You're a murderer, we all know it" first Host interaction, and quite a few of the Red Forest dialogue lines.
-Added in the "Please, close your eyes..." opening message from the original game that was previously left out of the remake.
-The opening stair descend room has new visual details/lighting.
-The room after the first save point has been DRASTICALLY reimagined.
-Finally up to NEC standards and put a warning sign up for the generator.
-Generator Room given some perspective (redesign).
-The foggy room where you first see Ghastly has a new audio detail added, as well as a strange force was cast upon the room.
-The Vine cracks made a little lighter in color.
-The staircase leading to the Subway puzzle has a new visual flourish.
-The Subway Station is now named.
-Erected a statue in the Subway station, added lights, pillars, and an employees only sign as well.
-"Do You Believe" now has a friend.
-You can now walk behind the red benches in the subway.
-Added some new flavor text and a small detail to the Subway stairs path.
-The giant hanging skull sprite has been reimagined.
-A not so delicious burger added.
-Hitbox of the cement mixer updated.
-In the second area of the Red Light death zone, made the exit a tiny bit more obvious.
-Updated the Tunnel Shape graffiti.
-Projector Puzzle made a tad bit easier with more clues.
-Hanging pods given a shadow to signify better than they're hanging from the ceiling.
-Added some flavor text to the caged entity in the Tunnel area stalker section.
-Added a dead rat to the tunnels. Cause why not?
-Added a few more creepy crawlies in the tunnels.
-Save point after the tunnels turned into a real dump.
-Sketchy Doodle Train section is now animated!
-Red Forest entrance now has a new sketchy look.
-Blood trail in the Red Forest section now looks better.
-The massacre ending in the Red Forest section now looks better too.
-The sobbing woman gives a little surprise now.
-Doubled the animation frames of the thing that crawls outta Little Marshmallow.
-Some punctuation fixes in the Red Forest art scene with Host.
-In the winter wonderland outside Judith Manor, the bushes got pricklier (and some turned into trees).
-Judith Manor now has wall trims.
-Judith Manor main hall now rounded out its staircase.
-The Yellow Diamond Key Door Sign now looks more like a yellow diamond.
-The Party Room in Judith Manor put up some more decorations.
-Some flavor text in the later parts of Judith Manor changed in subtle ways.
-Updated some sprites in the Forest section.
-New note added to Forest Cabin.
-Fixed up overgrowth and over-saturation of the floorboards in the Forest Cabin.
-Added some insect noises in the save area in the Forest.
-The exterior of the Forest Warehouse is a bit more overgrown now.
-Dummies no longer automatically take away a candle, there's now a new dummy death zone.
-Made the Forest Warehouse (Dummy Section) easier. You now need only 4 Talismans to leave, but getting all 6 Talismans gives you a reward.
-Remember not to play with fuses!
-Forest Warehouse has new visual flairs and touches.
-Forest Graveyard statue sprites updated.
-The Forest Gated Scarecrow path leading to the prison has been completely reimagined since the last update.
-The very first few rooms of the Prison added.


GIRLS GRAVEYARD:
-Added smoke to the chimneys.
-The purple water now moves.
-Redrew the "Arm Cut" CGs.
-Some decals added to the library room.
-Added a slight white flash to the Library Room transition, and to entering the Foggy Flower Field.
-In the section after the foggy flower field, but before the maze, added dripping sound effects that were in the original but forgotten in the remake, as well as darkened the whole place and made it foggier.
-Slight dialogue changes to the girl with purple hair.
-Added new story elements with new visuals to the "Sweet Note Scrawling" room after Round 6.
-Turned the audio down on the "Gargle Ghost" in the mirror breaking section.
-Fixed left & right entrances to the Darkness (previously were none).
-Added one new line of dialogue to the Boy's "Darkness" speech.
-Changed the way BGM speeds up in the Boy's "Darkness" speech.
-Turned down the audio in the Darkness secret.
-Bats in the Darkness section have a new sprite.
-Lightly altered some of the dialogue in the ending.


MY HOLE IS A MOUTH OF DIRT:
-Added some visual details to the entry tunnels after you speak to God and after you're instructed to go to God's Cradle.
-Mole's room has been adjusted, most notably a new sprite for his garbage bags full of cans.
-The water sprites in the sewer made to look more like water, and been littered with garbage.
-The sewer room with bars has new visual details.
-The door to Mole's chapel has been updated.
-Updated the Seeing Eye pictures in Mole's chapel, the pews in the chapel, along with new flavor text.
-The crosses in Mole's reading of the Book of Seeing made to stick out a tad bit more.
-Water stream in Mole's favorite spot in all of the sewer visually updated.
-Added cobwebs to Mole's emergency room.
-The furnace in the furnace room is now animated.
-Updated several pieces of graffiti in the tunnels because Gracen's a little bitch.
-A missing poster added with new flavor text.
-The pickaxe in the cramped dark room now casting a shadow, and the music doesn't restart when you loop in the room.
-Can now explore the whole bridge room.
-New tunnels appeared in the Mines.
-Two new cutscenes not in the original game added.
-New voiced version of previous cutscenes now in the game.
-Listen to a whole radio show if you wanna'.
-New achievement art.


GIRL'S GRAVEYARD MYSTERY:
-Added names above all the character dialogue boxes so you could more easily figure out who's talking.
-Changed Lotty's text color so it's easier to read.
-Altered  and added some dialogue with the villagers in the village before Round 3.
-Fixed the bug for the achievement in Round 3 to make it through without dying, it should work properly now.
-Added more new dialogue in the scene after Round 3.
-Fixed a few typos.
-Can now experience the entirety of the second dream sequence.


I hope y'all enjoy the update. This update actually took quite a lot of effort as been trying to raise the overall quality of the game. This wouldn't have been possible without the committed and helpful work from Gracen, who's been helping out a lot with Yai Gameworks project stuff lately. I'm grateful to him, and he's to thank for a lot of the new visuals (though a few dozen of the visual changes, especially the animated stuff, was still mostly me).

Still, on the to-do list that I'm hopeful to get around to somewhere in the first half of 2025, my priorities right now are:
-Get far more of Close Your Eyes done.
-Reimagine Close Your Eyes: The Twisted Puzzle.
-Finish My Hole is a Mouth of Dirt: Director's Cut
-Finish Girl's Graveyard Mystery.
-Get further in A Ghastly Tale.
-Add the secret second ending to Girl's Graveyard, and finish two currently unfinished secrets in Close Your Eyes.

To see how much of that I get done in the next update, but until then, I hope you guys enjoy the new form of Close Your Eyes Remake!

notes.title: Close Your Eyes Remake VER. 2.2 Update (Much New!)
notes.content:
Released an update for Close Your Eyes finally! This update mostly brings all the content in the game to its "Final" version. Close Your Eyes Remake saw the most additions, and I highly encourage replaying it from the start as there's honestly quite a few new sights, sounds, events, etc, to experience within it. The other game modes have also experienced smaller updates.

My Hole is a Mouth of Dirt: Director's Cut is also now officially starting, with the first section of it fully playable.

Here's a full list of patch notes:
ANNEX:
-Lowered the amount of achievements needed to unlock Twisted Puzzle (10 > 5), The Annex (5 > 0), A Ghastly Tale (20 > 15), and Beneath the Surface (35 > 30).
-Cleaned up the main annex lobby, put it into its "Final form" for layout, updated the dialogue around to properly reflect the update.

CLOSE YOUR EYES:
-Added a LOT of new sprites and details to various rooms.
-Added new flavor text to new details.
-Added some new events.
-Added some new secrets.
-Changed several Host voice lines to new recordings in the "New Voices" option, as I wasn't fully happy with several of the lines.
-Added new weed sprites for weed variety.
-Fixed up the "Hidden Hag Cassette" area with how it handled lighting a bit.
-Fixed some broken routes the enemies in the tunnel section can take.
-Fixed the "Death Zone" for the tunnel enemies if you died a second time (them spotting you wasn't reset previously).

GIRL'S GRAVEYARD:
-Fixed up some of the dialogue, some new lines added.
-Added a couple new secrets.
-Fixed a few typos.
-Made it so players could go back to get a selfie with the girl in red if they moved past it too quickly (can return to previous room).

Girl's Graveyard Mystery:
-Added a new event in the first night sequence.
-Fixed a few typos.
-Fixed the dialogue of some of the characters on Day 3 in the Village.

A Ghastly Tale:
-Added a few new sprite details/events.
-Fixed a few typos.
-The final room is a WIP, I know you can clip through the statue sprites and no flavor text currently. Just a work in progress for now.

My Hole is a Mouth of Dirt:
-Added properly.
-Voice acting added.
-One new room compared to the original in the current build.
-Various sprites updated to look better.
-Couple new hidden events to the OG.

The next update should be in October, I should be far more consistent from here on out.

notes.title: Yai Gameworks 2020 Questionnaire Survey
notes.content:
The Yai Gameworks 2020 Questionnaire Survey Form: [url=https://forms.gle/aAHSNATPVih4uDcK7]https://forms.gle/aAHSNATPVih4uDcK7[/url]

notes.title: Yai Gameworks upcoming game release plans and news
notes.content:
I thank you all who participated in the Yai Gameworks 2018 Questionnaire survey a couple months back. As many are probably aware of I am a man of many ideas, and indeed probably too many. I release 2-3 games a year but dates get pushed back, some are left idling for months to years before they eventually release. I won’t promise this won’t change, but as a solid effort applying some strategies I’ve learned within the last few months and a plight to achieve one of my dream games, Complete Isolation, I will explain a crazy thing I’m about to try and apply myself to do, then the reasoning, and finally the specifics.

Between February of 2018 to April of 2019 I want to release 12 video games onto Steam.

Now there’s a few reasons I have chosen to attempt this honestly foolish errand, especially foolish for me. I originally had set my sights to work on a dream project I’ve had in my head for many years, my first actual big project titled, “Complete Isolation.” I held a funding campaign for this game back in 2013 on Indiegogo, who’s funding has been used for all my projects to produce the music you all hear in my games. Still, here we are five years later and CI still does not exist. I want to make it, I desperately do, and I originally had planned to commit myself to it this year. That was until all my analysis, self-reflection, crunching, talking with others, and reason pointed me to pursuing another goal first, to do something else foolish first so that CI would be a less foolish endeavor and a safer bet.

You see, Complete Isolation is planned as an episodic gameplay experience. Episodic releases work best on a timed release manner; being timely with episodes is important. That means having a good groundwork you can easily build off of, self-discipline, a solid plan and commitment, and short development cycles. These are all things I need to master, and trying to wrangle that first-hand on an episodic game would be setting many up for disappointment of delays when I inevitability failed to deliver on time. I need to practice this first, but in a form that isn’t both as anti-consumer and as financially risky as a longer term episodic game. Climb a hill before a mountain kinda’ thing.

Add to this CI needs to look the part, it has a bigger investment, bigger cost, and as I’d be tackling a large chunk of the game myself from coding to design to music and writing and voice directing  I’d need someone to do the art, a pretty sizable amount of drawn art and sprite work as well. But the needed art amount is hefty, and I’m not in a financial position to offer a decent payment upfront. Rincs, my partner in crime on projects who’s done the drawn art on my projects, hasn’t seen a cent from Yai Gameworks sales and I feel awful about it. I need her for a longer term but don’t want to run her ragged, and need to pay her properly for her work. I should save up and split profits, but even that is a huge uncertainty. I need to secure more income, and allow her more time to do art for the project between her busy life.

Add to all of this having Yai Gameworks name out there and more experience under our belt can only be a good thing.

I decided to propose a challenge to myself, a series of experimental games on a planned and tight schedule. This is a way to work myself to a position where I can hopefully form the experience and conviction needed to do an episodic structure, all while getting more games and experiences under my belt. All while hopefully earning some money and making some more things available to all of you guys I hope that y’all enjoy. It may even work out to be a good way to market it as the steps up to try and achieve Complete Isolation.

There’s more to all of this. But I plan to in the upcoming week make a video detailing it all a little further. This plan isn’t just to make more games however, it’s to make an over-a-year plan and stick to it. The first game of this challenge is already released, it can be found as Please Love My Computer Game on Steam. However, I will now detail the rest of the plan to you all. I cannot guarantee I will be able to meet and achieve what I hope to, but I can tell you I’m going to be working hard to achieve my own dreams which I view this as a crucial step towards.

So if things pan out, what can you all expect?

APRIL 2018:
-”The Crack I Found That Taketh”
A nearly dialogue-less 3D exploration and discovery experimental game about a crack in the floor.

MAY 2018:
-”Red Haze” big content update
The big content update for Red Haze hits, including all endings, new areas, new story, new secrets, lag fixes, more scene skips, and more.

JUNE 2018:
-”Unlabeled”
An 8-bit game inspired by Hellnight and Nanashi no Game about an NPC in a small RPG village that one day gains sentience, and begins to be stalked by an ever-evolving monstrosity. Partner up with other people in the village that can permanently die at anytime, leading you down different storyline paths.

JULY 2018
-”Hellscape”
You are a Demigod on a dying world abandoned by the True Gods. Walk among men and explore the hellscape left behind,meeting devotees, non-believers, deformed and withering beings who may love or hate you. You may guide them to nurish a future, or trample them into oblivion. What gift may you give a disgusting world with no hope?

AUGUST 2018

notes.title: Yai Gameworks upcoming game release plans and news
notes.content:
I thank you all who participated in the Yai Gameworks 2018 Questionnaire survey a couple months back. As many are probably aware of I am a man of many ideas, and indeed probably too many. I release 2-3 games a year but dates get pushed back, some are left idling for months to years before they eventually release. I won’t promise this won’t change, but as a solid effort applying some strategies I’ve learned within the last few months and a plight to achieve one of my dream games, Complete Isolation, I will explain a crazy thing I’m about to try and apply myself to do, then the reasoning, and finally the specifics.

Between February of 2018 to April of 2019 I want to release 12 video games onto Steam.

Now there’s a few reasons I have chosen to attempt this honestly foolish errand, especially foolish for me. I originally had set my sights to work on a dream project I’ve had in my head for many years, my first actual big project titled, “Complete Isolation.” I held a funding campaign for this game back in 2013 on Indiegogo, who’s funding has been used for all my projects to produce the music you all hear in my games. Still, here we are five years later and CI still does not exist. I want to make it, I desperately do, and I originally had planned to commit myself to it this year. That was until all my analysis, self-reflection, crunching, talking with others, and reason pointed me to pursuing another goal first, to do something else foolish first so that CI would be a less foolish endeavor and a safer bet.

You see, Complete Isolation is planned as an episodic gameplay experience. Episodic releases work best on a timed release manner; being timely with episodes is important. That means having a good groundwork you can easily build off of, self-discipline, a solid plan and commitment, and short development cycles. These are all things I need to master, and trying to wrangle that first-hand on an episodic game would be setting many up for disappointment of delays when I inevitability failed to deliver on time. I need to practice this first, but in a form that isn’t both as anti-consumer and as financially risky as a longer term episodic game. Climb a hill before a mountain kinda’ thing.

Add to this CI needs to look the part, it has a bigger investment, bigger cost, and as I’d be tackling a large chunk of the game myself from coding to design to music and writing and voice directing  I’d need someone to do the art, a pretty sizable amount of drawn art and sprite work as well. But the needed art amount is hefty, and I’m not in a financial position to offer a decent payment upfront. Rincs, my partner in crime on projects who’s done the drawn art on my projects, hasn’t seen a cent from Yai Gameworks sales and I feel awful about it. I need her for a longer term but don’t want to run her ragged, and need to pay her properly for her work. I should save up and split profits, but even that is a huge uncertainty. I need to secure more income, and allow her more time to do art for the project between her busy life.

Add to all of this having Yai Gameworks name out there and more experience under our belt can only be a good thing.

I decided to propose a challenge to myself, a series of experimental games on a planned and tight schedule. This is a way to work myself to a position where I can hopefully form the experience and conviction needed to do an episodic structure, all while getting more games and experiences under my belt. All while hopefully earning some money and making some more things available to all of you guys I hope that y’all enjoy. It may even work out to be a good way to market it as the steps up to try and achieve Complete Isolation.

There’s more to all of this. But I plan to in the upcoming week make a video detailing it all a little further. This plan isn’t just to make more games however, it’s to make an over-a-year plan and stick to it. The first game of this challenge is already released, it can be found as Please Love My Computer Game on Steam. However, I will now detail the rest of the plan to you all. I cannot guarantee I will be able to meet and achieve what I hope to, but I can tell you I’m going to be working hard to achieve my own dreams which I view this as a crucial step towards.

So if things pan out, what can you all expect?

A nearly dialogue-less 3D exploration and discovery experimental game about a crack in the floor.

Thanks to the wonderful feedback on the Yai Gameworks 2018 Questionnaire and some wonderful occurrences that happened towards the end of 2017, I'm here to announce a finalized date for the release of the early access for Close Your Eyes -Anniversary Remake-. The early access version of the game will release on January 24th, 2017 for the price of $4.99, though with a 5% discount for the first week of launch (and an additional 5% off for 10% total if you buy through the Yai Gameworks Complete Bundle).

The Early Access includes the full remakes of Close Your Eyes and Girl's Graveyard within them at launch, fully completed and playable from start to finish for all possible endings and secrets. The price will raise by a bit right before the game leaves Early Access, but I will announce when that is ahead of time. I am aiming for August 31st as the release out of Early Access, but to prepare for potential delays the latest may be September 28th.

If you're curious about the Red Haze content update, it will release before the end of April 2018 I promise. Found Horror Game 11.exe also will definitely release sometime before CYE -AR- comes out of Early Access. notes.title: Close Your Eyes -Anniversary Remake- releasing on April 27th, 2018
notes.content:
http://store.steampowered.com/app/706710/Close_Your_Eyes_Anniversary_Remake/

Close Your Eyes -Anniversary Remake- will be releasing on April 27th, 2018, which is the 4-year anniversary of the original Close Your Eyes releasing for Ludum Dare, and the 3-year anniversary of the original Redux version. The remake includes 5 scenarios, including a remade Close Your Eyes and Girl's Graveyard which polishes the game further, adds new areas, new threats, new story, and new surprises to both. It also includes an 'Anniversary Twist' on both in a new scenario, and a complete brand new scenario known as 'Beneath the Surface', as well as a hub with secrets that connects all five scenarios together.

The remake will release for $4.99 USD, and I hope it surprises a lot of you. I'll have more information early next year, but a few blurbs I can share is the Remake between all of its scenarios should be 7-16 hour experience, there is around 30 new pieces of artwork for new story scenes done by Rincs for the title, there's 100 Steam Achievements (and most of them I tried to make interesting to get), and some segments of the original game have also been greatly redone and changed (two examples I can give, the Judith Manor Key Collecting section has been entirely redone in a new (and in my opinion, much better) way, as well as a completely new path if you choose to leave the manor, and similarly there's a new path instead of doing the train puzzle in the early parts of CYE, but the train puzzle path has a lot new to it as well).

Hope you all look forward to it!
